approach: Add `check_subjective_method(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs and one `step!(check_subjective_method(reading, request));` line at the end of `refusing_check` (after `check_reading_references`, so no pinned adjacency test moves). The check finds a subjective-quality outcome in the request's plain prose (existing `plain_request_prose` and `plain_line` in terms.rs, which drop quoted spans, paths, example lists and generated lines) or in the reading summary: a whole-word subjective phrase (newcomer, clear to/for, how clear, clarity, easy to follow/understand/read, understandable, readable) on the same line as an audience-facing artifact noun (page, document, docs, guide, explainer, readme, tutorial, article, site, manual). It refuses unless ONE criterion names all four parts of a method: an independent or fresh model reader that had no part in building the work, a persona, a 1 to 5 rating, and a pass threshold. The error names the missing parts and says to state the method before the build. Requests holding the root-cause anchor are skipped, since the cited failure is the subject of the fix. Root cause named in the doc comment: no required verification method for subjective quality at the reading gate (jobs 20261014-163844-c2kt and 20261015-064153-wekz). Tests: unit tests in reading.rs, refusal-corpus cases with input-form tags, a doc/changelog/declared-share corpus test, a reading-rules line in briefs.rs, a CHANGELOG entry and a C8 row in defaults-loop.md section 3.6. Criterion 8 (fmt, clippy, test) is shown by the three whole-repo commands, each tied to a named failure that happens if the change is missing or incomplete (see the demonstration).

decisions.choice: Put the check at the reading gate as one new `step!` line at the end of `refusing_check`, not in any prompt, defaults.toml or either job's code.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading with a subjective outcome and no method is accepted (`refusing_check`, checks.rs). `check_reading_acceptance` is the one gate for the build path (reading.rs:679), the text-only replay and `athena check-reading` (replay.rs:55), so one step covers all. The corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. Appending at the end keeps the adjacency tests (governance→outcome, outcome→reach, reach→defined_terms, survey→history_fixture) passing.

rejected.why: The reader set has 3 tokens of headroom, defaults.toml is governance and not a deliverable, and prose does not refuse a reading (defaults `mechanism`).

rejected.option: Redo the newcomer.rs gate in athena-cap-study or wire the audience rating into the ship path
rejected.why: Out of scope in the brief; those act after the build, and the cause is at admission.

rejected.option: Insert the step next to check_outcome_state
rejected.why: Tests assert exact neighbours of several steps; inserting there breaks them.

decisions.choice: Trigger only when a subjective phrase and an artifact noun sit on the same line of plain prose (reusing `plain_request_prose`/`plain_line`); read the reading summary through `plain_line` too.
decisions.reason: Criterion 6: ordinary code requests must not be refused. Bare 'clear' ('clear the cache') and 'human-readable output' have no artifact noun. `plain_request_prose` already drops quoted spans, backtick spans, paths, example lists and generated lines.

rejected.option: Trigger on any occurrence of 'clear' or 'readable'
rejected.why: Would refuse 'clear the cache' and 'human-readable output'; fails criterion 6.

rejected.option: Ask a model to classify whether the outcome is subjective
rejected.why: Adds a model call to a deterministic gate; every sibling check is deterministic.

decisions.choice: Skip the check when the request holds `ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR` ("The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.").
decisions.reason: This job's own request and any future root-cause fix for this class quote 'a page is clear to a newcomer' as the cause; the reading changes code and must not be refused for the cited failure. terms.rs uses the same anchor for the same reason. Limit stated in the doc comment.

rejected.option: Scan root-cause requests like any other
rejected.why: Would refuse this very job on a retry, and any fix to the check.

decisions.choice: Satisfied by one criterion (any kind) holding all four parts; the error names the parts missing from the closest criterion (most parts; all four if none). Detection is lowercase phrase matching: independent (independent, fresh, 'no part in', 'did not build', separate) with (reader, model, reviewer, judge); persona (persona, 'as a ', 'as an ', newcomer, novice, beginner); scale ('1 to 5', '1-5', en dash, 'out of 5', '/5', '5-point', 'five-point'); threshold (at least, minimum, below, 'or above', 'or higher', threshold, blocks, 'no less than') plus a digit.
decisions.reason: A method is one check; parts spread over criteria give no single check a verifier can run. Persona is in the brief's accepted reading and the outcome-check default.

rejected.option: Accept parts spread across several criteria
rejected.why: No single criterion tells a verifier how to rate; the error could not name what is missing.

rejected.option: Require the threshold to be at least 4
rejected.why: The user did not ask the gate to fix a number; left as an open question.

decisions.choice: Add a tenth reading rule to `READING_RULES` in briefs.rs and update its test (count 9→10, check list, byte bound 2750→3000 with the measured size in the comment).
decisions.reason: briefs.rs is a listed deliverable and the rules list names every check. The reader budget set is CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and catalog (crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs), not the brief, so the 3-token headroom is untouched.

rejected.why: The reader would learn the rule only from the refusal.

decisions.choice: Show criterion 8 with the three whole-repo check commands and tie each to a concrete failure the change would cause if incomplete, rather than a vague 'all pass'.
decisions.reason: Findings 1 and 2: a behavior criterion needs fails_without and a named seam. The checks are the production gate commands Athena itself runs; the seam is the repository's own workspace and test suites, which exist today.

open_questions: User: Should the check later require the stated pass threshold to be at least 4 of 5, as the outcome-check default says, or is any stated threshold enough? This plan accepts any stated threshold and only requires that one exists.
